title: More Math Tricks
story: You're at a restaurant with your family. The bill is $60, tax is 8%, and you want to add a 15% tip. Figuring out the total means doing several math steps in the right order � exactly what parentheses help with!
why: Parentheses control the order of math operations, just like in real math class � they make sure your program calculates correctly every time.
analogy: Parentheses in math are like fences around a group of things � everything inside gets handled first, as a team.
try_it: Calculate (10 + 5) * 3 versus 10 + 5 * 3 and print both. Then try (20 - 8) / 2 versus 20 - 8 / 2. See how parentheses change everything!
tips: When in doubt, add parentheses � they make your intention crystal clear and prevent bugs!
XIOM follows the same math rules you learned in school: PEMDAS (Parentheses, Exponents, Multiply/Divide, Add/Subtract)
You can nest parentheses: `((a + b) * c) / d` � the innermost pair goes first
common_mistakes: Forgetting that division of two Int values drops the decimal � `7 / 2` gives `3`, not `3.5`
Writing unbalanced parentheses like `(a + b * c` � every `(` needs a matching `)`
